mathematical_and_spec_reasoning: The existing raw magnitude bound is inclusive |x|<=2^120 (0x7b800000). It rejects all larger finite values, infinities and NaNs before construction. Dropping it or substituting only isfinite would be invalid. RTInvalid behavior remains exact.

For bounded finite nonzero binary32 x, the usual ordered IEEE/RTE/gradual-underflow chain has five value-pairs (0,0),(x,0),(0,0),(x,0),(0,0). Addition of zero is exact; cancellation residuals are zero; no overflow, discarded magnitude or nonzero arithmetic radius occurs. Either input zero sign has the valid canonical all-positive-zero result. Direct construction retains the represented x and radius0/valid1.

The ordinary native entrypoint has RTE32/DenormPreserve32 and NoContraction but not SignedZeroInfNanPreserve32. Vulkan assumes NSZ/NotInf/NotNaN in that environment. NoContraction prevents its specified arithmetic rearrangement permissions; it does not independently require signed-zero preservation.

Consequently the specified literal-positive-zero result is a valid refinement of the allowed constructor behavior. This is a value/allowed-behavior argument, not proof that every baseline driver lowering emits those identical zero words. An existential allowed result and universal equality to every lowering are different requirements.

No actual counterexample or differing device result has been established. Missing universal zero-word proof does not itself establish inequivalence. Downstream bitcasts/sign-bit operations make actual zero words observable, so concrete raw-word checks cannot be dismissed using NSZ.
